title: Patient characteristics to guide personalized treatment decisions and prognostication in hepatocellular carcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Patient characteristics to guide personalized treatment decisions and prognostication in hepatocellular carcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for approximately 90% of primary liver cancer cases and is the fourth leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with over a million annual deaths predicted by 2030 [1]. The global burden of hepatocellular carcinoma continues to rise, with marked geographic variability reflecting differences in underlying etiologies and screening practices [2]. About 90% of HCC cases are seen in cirrhotic livers, which are typically associated with obesity, alcoholism and chronic hepatitis infections [3]. As the etiologic landscape changes due to public health initiatives like HBV vaccination and HCV antiviral therapy, an epidemiological shift toward non-viral causes is beginning to emerge [4,5]. Moreover, the global rise in obesity as a pandemic disease due to sedentary lifestyle and changing dietary habits has resulted in an increasing prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and its progression to cirrhosis [4,5]. Despite advances in surveillance strategies, a substantial proportion of patients continue to present with advanced-stage disease, limiting the applicability of curative therapies such as resection, transplantation, or ablation. Consequently, HCC remains a major contributor to global cancer-related mortality, with disproportionately poor outcomes in resource-limited settings.

【Introduction · S0001-p2】HCC is unique among solid malignancies because treatment decisions must account for both tumor burden and underlying liver function. Tumor burden should be characterized using reproducible imaging metrics. RECIST 1.1, which is commonly used in prospective systemic therapy trials, evaluates changes in the size of selected target lesions, whereas modified RECIST (mRECIST) evaluates viable HCC by measuring the arterial-phase enhancing component of the tumor [6,7]. Volumetric tumor measurements may provide additional information but remain less standardized for routine systemic treatment decisions

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Patient characteristics to guide personalized treatment decisions and prognostication in hepatocellular carcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methodology · S0001-S2001-p3】As this manuscript was designed as a narrative review rather than a systematic review, formal inclusion and exclusion criteria were not prespecified. Priority was given to phase II and III clinical trials, guideline recommendations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses and high-quality real-world studies evaluating patient-specific prognostic factors and treatment outcomes.

【Methodology · S0001-S2001-p4】The real-world evidence included in this review was heterogeneous in design and methodological quality, ranging from prospective multicenter registries to retrospective single-center cohorts. Interpretation considered sample size, patient selection, geographic setting, treatment era, completeness of follow-up, consistency of outcome definitions, and the potential for confounding by indication, immortal-time bias, and missing data. Because a formal risk-of-bias tool was not applied, real-world estimates were considered complementary and hypothesis-generating and were not assigned the same evidentiary weight as randomized clinical-trial results. Reported efficacy and safety outcomes were extracted directly from original publications and interpreted within the context of individual study design and eligibility criteria.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Patient characteristics to guide personalized treatment decisions and prognostication in hepatocellular carcinoma》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Historical standards · S0001-S2002-p2】Sorafenib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, which targets the VEGFR 1–3, PDGFR-β, and RAF-MEK-ERK signaling cascade [10,17,18]. It was approved as a systemic therapy for advanced HCC based on SHARP trial [3,10]. This trial demonstrated a median overall survival (mOS) of 10.7 months (95% CI 9.4–13.3) versus 7.9 months with placebo (95% CI 6.8–9.1; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55–0.87) and median progression free survival (PFS) of 5.5 months (95% CI 4.1–6.9) versus 2.8 months (95% CI 2.7–3.9); HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.74) [10]. This was a significant 31% relative reduction in the hazard of death and a 2.8-month absolute improvement in median overall survival. Thus, the benefit was clinically meaningful in a setting with no effective systemic alternative, although the absolute median survival gain remained modest. For more than a decade, sorafenib was the only approved frontline systemic therapy for unresectable HCC [10,17,18].

【Historical standards · S0001-S2002-p3】The REFLECT trial evaluated lenvatinib, an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR 1–3, FGFR 1–4, PDGFR-α, RET, and KIT, as a non-inferior treatment option to sorafenib, demonstrating mOS of 13.6 months (95% CI 12.1–14.9) versus 12.3 months with sorafenib (95% CI 10.4–13.9; HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79–1.06), while also significantly prolonging PFS to 7.4 months (95% CI 6.9–8.8) vs 3.7 months (95% CI 3.6–4.6); HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.57–0.77) [3,12, 19–21].
